findings.title: Slots inside a date override bypass busy-time checks
findings.body: When a slot is on a date-override day and inside the override window, the find callback returns nothing, dateOverrideExist is true, and checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 134 without reaching the busy.every() check at the bottom. A fixed or round-robin host can therefore be shown/booked during a date-override slot even when they have an accepted Cal booking or a busy calendar event overlapping that slot.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects slots covered by any non-first range and uses wrong end/day
findings.body: This block returns unavailable if ANY workingHour entry for that weekday does not contain the slot (find on start<startTime||end>endTime), instead of checking whether NO entry contains it. Users with split/multiple ranges on the same day will lose slots covered by a later range. Additionally end at line 142 is copied from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so a slot starting inside working hours but ending after endTime passes, and both day()/hour() are taken from the UTC slot time while WorkingHours days/startTime/endTime are expressed in the organizer's schedule timezone, so non-UTC hosts are compared on the wrong day and hour.

findings.title: Empty date-override comparison uses object identity and never matches
findings.body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, so the intended zero-length override (whole day unavailable) branch is dead. A slot that straddles the equal start/end instant then falls through both boundary checks, sets dateOverrideExist, and is returned as available instead of unavailable.

findings.title: Date override shifted across midnight is truncated/wrong-day
findings.body: startTime/endTime are derived only from hour()*60+minute() after adding the invitee-organizer offset. If the offset pushes the override across midnight (common when organizer and invitee are on opposite sides of the date line), endTime can become smaller than startTime or both wrap to the next day's clock time while activeOverrides still matched the override against the unshifted invitee day at line 207. buildSlots discards start>=end boundaries, so such overrides disappear or appear on the wrong day.

findings.title: No test for the round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
findings.body: The PR description claims fixed hosts' date overrides are now honoured for round-robin events, but the only added test re-queries the existing personal-event date-override scenario in Asia/Dhaka and expects identical UTC slots. There is no scenario with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN, a fixed host with an override, and a loose host, nor a case where the fixed host's calendar/booking conflicts inside the override, so the new checkIfIsAvailable filtering for fixed/loose hosts is untested and the busy-bypass regression above would not be caught.
